name: Hevy Pro
tagline: Log workouts and routines locally with neutral progress charts

pricing.notes: Annual Pro plan divided by 12; monthly billing is higher.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 4 routines, 7 custom exercises, and stats history limited to 30 days or 3 months depending on view; 400+ built-in exercises
tiers.notes: Only weight and waist measurements remain available on the free account.

tiers.name: Hevy Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited routines and custom exercises plus all-time graph/history access
tiers.notes: $23.99 billed annually; the US App Store also exposes a $3.99 monthly offer for some users.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free plan: 4 routines, 7 custom exercises, 30-day/3-month statistics windows, and 400+ built-in exercises.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual + one-time Lifetime; app-store offers can vary
pricing.hiddenCosts: Hevy Coach is a separate product and can create a second subscription. App-store legacy/alternate monthly offers can differ from the public $2.99 rate.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Hevy Pro, log workouts and routines locally with neutral progress charts. The hard boundary is mobile apps, social features, watch integration, sync, and polished tracking, plus hardware data, content, coaching, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Log workouts and routines locally, plan moderate training, and show neutral progress charts without diagnosing, shaming, or enforcing restrictive goals.
requirements: optional HealthKit or Health Connect permission
whatYouLose: mobile apps, social features, watch integration, sync, and polished tracking
large content library and social network
moatNotes: hardware data, content, coaching, and trust
ongoingBurden: sensor permissions, data quality, notifications, safety language, accessibility, sync, privacy, content review, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Hevy Pro because people pay for polished mobile capture, trusted content, hardware integration, and coaching rather than the basic logbook. The recurring cost buys sensor permissions, data quality, notifications, safety language, accessibility, sync, privacy, content review, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: wger
priorArt.desc: Active open-source fitness and workout management application.

alternatives.name: LiftLog
alternatives.desc: Sets, timers, plans and charts live on the phone instead of behind a lifetime unlock.

facts.install: Install the iOS or Android app from an app store
facts.engines: The optional paid routine generator uses Anthropic Claude; normal workout logging and charts do not require an AI service.
facts.dataFormat: Workout plans, exercise history, sets, and measurements are kept on the device and can be exported as plaintext; optional social/backup features publish encrypted data through the project's backend.
facts.gapVsPaid: LiftLog lacks Hevy's large social community, polished exercise discovery, coaching-style routine marketplace, wearable integrations, and cross-platform sharing experience.

alternatives.name: FitNotes
alternatives.desc: A no-ad Android lifting log that has been doing the basic job for years.

facts.install: Install the Android app from Google Play
facts.dataFormat: Workout routines, exercise history, measurements, and notes live in the app's local database; optional backups can be written to the user's Google Drive.
facts.gapVsPaid: FitNotes is Android-only and gives up Hevy's iOS/web presence, social feed, friend comparisons, richer exercise media, and polished cloud synchronization.

alternatives.name: wger
alternatives.desc: Workouts, sets, timers and charts on your own server; setup day counts as cardio.

facts.install: Create an account on wger.de/use the mobile app, or deploy the official Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: Hosted records live in wger's service; self-hosted users keep accounts, workouts, nutrition, measurements, and exercise data in PostgreSQL plus persistent media volumes, while the mobile client maintains an offline local database and syncs.
facts.gapVsPaid: wger is broader but its logging flow, exercise media, offline/mobile polish, social layer, and instant setup are less refined than Hevy's.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the hosted service or mobile app; self-hosting immediately requires Docker Compose, PostgreSQL, Redis/sync services, a reverse proxy, mail, backups, and upgrades.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal general-wellbeing tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Hevy Pro in an empty repository.
Use React Native with Expo, TypeScript, SQLite, and HealthKit or Health Connect only when explicitly enabled; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: log workouts and routines locally, plan moderate training, and show neutral progress charts without diagnosing, shaming, or enforcing restrictive goals.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create optional logs for activity, sleep, mood, energy, and personal notes with editable units.
Let the user build moderate routines and rest days without weight-loss targets, punishment, or competitive pressure.
Request health-platform permissions per data type and work fully without granting them.
Show weekly patterns and consistency with neutral language and no diagnostic or body-image judgments.
Add reminders that can be muted, data export, account-free local use, and full deletion.
Include a clear statement that the app is not medical care and should not replace qualified advice.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out medical diagnosis or treatment.
Deliberately leave out extreme exercise or restrictive-eating coaching.
Deliberately leave out wearable hardware, human coaching, and a large social network.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
